name: Contrast ratio
definition: A number from 1:1 to 21:1 describing how far apart two colours sit in relative luminance, used to decide whether text on a background is readable.
useWhen: measuring whether two colours are far enough apart to read
notes: Head term. Cross-category with accessibility; kept in color because the demo is two swatches and a number.

name: Relative luminance
definition: The brightness of a colour measured on a 0 to 1 scale after each channel is linearised, which is the input every WCAG contrast calculation actually uses.
useWhen: explaining why two colours of equal saturation contrast differently
notes: Tail. The reason yellow and blue at the same HSL lightness score wildly different contrast.

name: APCA
definition: A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.
useWhen: scoring contrast in a way that accounts for text size and weight

sources.title: Radix Colors: understanding the scale (quotes Lc 60 and Lc 90)

notes: Tail gold: Radix guarantees its step 11 and 12 text against step 2 in Lc, not in WCAG ratio.

name: Hue
definition: The attribute that gives a colour its name, red or teal or violet, expressed as an angle around a colour wheel independent of how light or vivid it is.
useWhen: naming the colour itself, apart from its lightness or intensity

name: Saturation
definition: How far a colour is from grey on a scale where 100 percent is the pure hue and 0 percent is neutral, as modelled by HSL and its relatives.
useWhen: describing how vivid or washed out a colour looks
notes: Merge candidate with chroma; they are not the same measure and the distinction is worth a contrastWith edge.

name: Chroma
definition: Colourfulness measured in absolute terms rather than as a percentage of the maximum, so a light pastel and a dark ink can be compared on one scale.
useWhen: comparing colourfulness across colours of different lightness
notes: The word that separates OKLCH from HSL: chroma is unbounded and hue dependent, saturation is a percentage.

name: Lightness
definition: How light or dark a colour reads, from black at one end to white at the other, held separately from its hue and its colourfulness.
useWhen: stepping a colour lighter or darker without changing the hue
notes: Brightness, value, lightness and tone are four vocabularies for nearby ideas; disambiguation prose is the point of this entry.

name: Tint
definition: A colour with white mixed in, lighter than the original hue and used for faint fills, hover washes and subtle backgrounds.
useWhen: a lighter version of a colour made by adding white
notes: Apple overloads 'tint colour' to mean the app accent colour, which is a genuine naming dispute worth calling out.

name: Shade
definition: A colour with black mixed in, darker than the original hue and typically used for pressed states, borders and dark theme surfaces.
useWhen: a darker version of a colour made by adding black
notes: Casual usage calls every ramp step a 'shade'; the entry should note the strict versus loose sense.

name: Tone
definition: A colour with grey mixed in, softer than the pure hue, and in Material's vocabulary the numbered lightness step from 0 to 100 that a palette is built from.
useWhen: a muted colour, or a numbered lightness step in Material

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

notes: Two live senses (paint mixing versus Material tone); merge candidate with lightness if canonicalize prefers one entry.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of lightness

name: Color wheel
definition: A circular arrangement of hues that makes relationships between colours geometric, so a scheme becomes a shape drawn across the circle.
useWhen: picking colours by their angular relationship to each other

name: Color harmony
definition: A rule for choosing colours by their positions on the wheel, such as complementary or analogous or triadic, so a palette holds together by construction.
useWhen: choosing a palette by a geometric rule rather than by eye

sources.title: The Ultimate Color Glossary For UI Designers

name: Complementary colors
definition: Two hues sitting opposite each other on the colour wheel, the pairing that produces the strongest contrast and the loudest accent.
useWhen: the loudest possible pairing of two hues
notes: Split-complementary is recorded here as an alias; canonicalize may promote it to its own entry.

name: Analogous colors
definition: A palette built from hues that neighbour each other on the wheel, giving a calm scheme with no colour fighting another for attention.
useWhen: a quiet palette of neighbouring hues

name: Triadic color scheme
definition: A palette of three hues spaced evenly around the colour wheel, vivid by construction and usually applied with one hue dominant.
useWhen: three hues balanced evenly around the wheel

name: Monochromatic palette
definition: A scheme drawn from one hue at many lightness and saturation levels, so hierarchy comes from contrast alone rather than from colour difference.
useWhen: one hue carrying the whole interface

sources.title: The Ultimate Color Glossary For UI Designers

name: Color temperature
definition: Whether a colour reads warm (toward red and orange) or cool (toward blue), the axis designers use to bias a neutral grey without changing its lightness.
useWhen: biasing a palette warm or cool

name: 60-30-10 rule
definition: A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.
useWhen: deciding how much of each colour to use, not which colours
notes: Tail gold: names the question 'how much of each colour', which no token system answers.

name: Accent color
definition: The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.
useWhen: the one colour reserved for the primary action
notes: The CSS accent-color property (which tints checkboxes and range inputs) is a distinct enough sense that it may deserve its own tail entry.

name: Brand color
definition: The colour an organisation owns in a customer's memory, carried into a product as the seed for its palette rather than used directly on every surface.
useWhen: the colour the company owns, before it becomes UI tokens

name: Neutral palette
definition: The greys an interface is mostly made of, ramped from page background to body text, which carry the structure while the accent carries the attention.
useWhen: the greys that most of the interface is actually made of

name: Tinted neutral
definition: A grey with a trace of the brand hue mixed in, so backgrounds and borders belong to the palette instead of reading as a separate, colder system.
useWhen: greys that quietly carry the brand hue
notes: Tail gold: readers search 'why does my grey look dirty next to my blue'.

name: Status color
definition: The small fixed set of colours a product reserves for outcome, typically success, warning, danger and info, so meaning is consistent wherever it appears.
useWhen: colours that report an outcome rather than a brand
notes: Merge candidate with the existing semantic-color stub; status colour is the narrower, outcome-only sense.

name: Surface color
definition: The colour of a plane that content sits on, defined as a set of stacked levels so a card on a page and a sheet on a card are told apart by value.
useWhen: naming the plane content sits on, not the page background

name: On-color
definition: A colour defined by what it sits on, such as on-primary or on-surface, so every fill ships with the foreground guaranteed to be readable against it.
useWhen: the foreground colour that ships paired with a fill

implementations.name: On primary, On surface, On error

notes: Tail gold: the 'on' prefix is opaque to newcomers and is exactly the kind of word this site exists to answer.

name: Container color
definition: A muted companion to an accent, light enough to fill a chip or a card behind ordinary text, so an accent can shade a region without shouting.
useWhen: a soft fill in the accent hue rather than the solid accent

name: Color role
definition: A named job in the interface, such as surface or outline or on-primary, that components style themselves against instead of reaching for a palette value.
useWhen: the job a colour does, as the thing components reference
notes: Strong merge candidate with the existing semantic-color stub; role is the system's word, semantic colour is the community's.

name: State layer
definition: A translucent sheet of the content colour laid over a control at a fixed opacity per state, so hover, focus and pressed are one rule instead of three palettes.
useWhen: one overlay opacity expressing hover, focus and pressed
notes: Tail gold and very demoable: one swatch, four states, opacity readout.

name: Surface tint
definition: A wash of the primary colour blended into a surface in proportion to its elevation, so height reads as a colour shift rather than only as a shadow.
useWhen: elevation shown by tinting a surface rather than by shadow

name: Elevation overlay
definition: The older dark theme technique of laying white over a surface at an opacity that rises with elevation, because shadows are nearly invisible on dark backgrounds.
useWhen: raising a dark surface where a shadow would not show
notes: Superseded by surface tint in Material 3; the entry should say so, since both words are still in circulation.

name: Scrim
definition: A translucent or gradient layer laid over imagery or behind a dialog, dimming what is beneath so text on top clears contrast or so focus moves forward.
useWhen: darkening what is behind so the layer above stays readable
notes: Tail gold. Classic 'what is the word for the dark gradient behind the caption on a photo'.

name: Inverse color
definition: A surface and text pair flipped against the current theme, so a snackbar or tooltip reads as a foreign object that arrived from outside the page.
useWhen: an element deliberately styled opposite to the theme

implementations.name: Inverse surface, Inverse on surface, Inverse primary

name: Dark mode
definition: A second palette built on dark surfaces with light foregrounds, derived from the light one by rebalancing lightness and saturation rather than by inverting it.
useWhen: the dark counterpart of a palette, not an inversion of it
notes: Head term. The interesting content is the rules that make a dark palette not an inversion: reduced saturation, no pure white text.

name: True black theme
definition: A dark palette whose background is pure black rather than near black, which switches OLED pixels off entirely but makes elements look like they float in a void.
useWhen: a dark theme at pure black for OLED, not near black
notes: Tail. Names the argument about #000000 versus #121212 that every dark theme discussion reaches.

name: Flash of inaccurate color theme
definition: The moment a page paints in the wrong theme before the stored preference is applied, showing a light flash to a reader who chose dark.
useWhen: the wrong theme showing for a frame on page load

sources.title: Avoiding Flash of Inaccurate Theme Color

notes: Tail gold with a real community acronym. Demo is document scope (first paint of a whole document), hence iframe.

name: Forced colors mode
definition: An operating system mode that replaces a page's palette with a small user-chosen set of system colours, overriding almost everything an author specified.
useWhen: the OS is imposing its own palette on your interface

sources.title: Styling for Windows high contrast with forced colors

notes: Cross-category with accessibility; kept in color because the subject is the palette substitution itself.

name: Increased contrast preference
definition: A user setting asking for stronger separation between foreground and background, which platforms expose so a product can ship a higher contrast palette.
useWhen: the reader has asked the system for more contrast

sources.title: Material 3: color overview (standard, medium and high contrast)

notes: Cross-category with accessibility. Material ships medium and high contrast palettes alongside light and dark.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of prefers-contrast

name: Color scheme
definition: The declaration that a page or element supports light or dark rendering, which also tells the browser which palette to use for scrollbars and form controls.
useWhen: telling the browser which themes your page supports
notes: Demo is arguably document scope, since the visible effect includes the document scrollbar and UA form widgets.

name: light-dark()
definition: A CSS function that takes two colours and returns the one matching the page's current colour scheme, collapsing a theme's light and dark values into one declaration.
useWhen: writing both theme values inline instead of in a media query

name: Color space
definition: A coordinate system for describing colour, where the choice of axes decides whether arithmetic like mixing or stepping a ramp matches what the eye sees.
useWhen: naming the coordinate system a colour value is written in
notes: Colour space versus colour model is a live distinction worth the disambiguation prose.

name: OKLCH
definition: A colour notation of lightness, chroma and hue built on Oklab, where changing the hue leaves the perceived lightness alone and equal steps look equal.
useWhen: writing colour so that equal numeric steps look equal

name: HCT
definition: Material's colour space of hue, chroma and tone, which borrows hue and chroma from CAM16 and lightness from CIELAB so tone alone predicts contrast.
useWhen: generating a Material palette where tone predicts contrast

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

notes: Tail gold: the reason Material can promise a contrast ratio from a tone number alone.

name: Perceptual uniformity
definition: The property of a colour space where equal numeric distances look like equal visual differences, which is what makes a generated ramp step evenly.
useWhen: explaining why an HSL ramp looks uneven and an OKLCH one does not

name: Color gamut
definition: The set of colours a space or a display can actually produce, which is why a value that is legal in one notation can be impossible on a given screen.
useWhen: asking whether a colour can be shown at all

name: Wide gamut
definition: Colour beyond what sRGB can express, addressed in CSS through spaces such as display-p3 and rec2020 and shown only on displays that reach that far.
useWhen: reaching for colours sRGB cannot express

sources.title: Wide Gamut Color in CSS with Display-P3

notes: Radix notes alpha blending differs in P3 from sRGB, which is a good disambiguation hook.

name: Gamut mapping
definition: Converting a colour that falls outside a display's range into the nearest one inside it, usually by lowering chroma in OKLCH rather than clipping each channel.
useWhen: bringing an impossible colour into a display's range
notes: Tail gold: clipping darkens a bright colour, mapping does not, and that difference is visible in a demo.

name: sRGB
definition: The default colour space of the web, the one hex codes and plain rgb() values live in, and the baseline every wider gamut is described relative to.
useWhen: the assumed colour space behind a hex code

name: Hex color
definition: A colour written as a hash followed by three, four, six or eight hexadecimal digits, the notation most handoffs still speak even when the source is OKLCH.
useWhen: the notation a colour is handed over in
notes: The 8-digit form (hex with alpha) is the part people actually search for.

name: Opacity
definition: How much of what is behind an element shows through it, applied to the whole element and its children at once rather than to a single colour value.
useWhen: fading an entire element and everything inside it
notes: Merge candidate with alpha-channel; the useful entry is the contrast between them, so both records should survive as a contrastWith pair.

name: Alpha channel
definition: The transparency component carried inside a colour value itself, which lets a border or fill blend with whatever surface it lands on instead of assuming one.
useWhen: a colour that must blend with an unknown background

name: Alpha compositing
definition: The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.
useWhen: predicting the result of stacking translucent layers
notes: Premultiplied versus straight alpha is a strong candidate for its own tail entry if canonicalize wants the split.

name: Blend mode
definition: A formula for combining a layer's colour with the colour behind it, such as multiply or screen or overlay, instead of simply covering it.
useWhen: combining layers by a formula rather than by covering
notes: The isolation property (stopping a blend at a stacking context) is a plausible separate tail entry.

name: Duotone
definition: An image rendered in two colours instead of full colour, mapping its shadows to one hue and its highlights to another so photography joins the brand palette.
useWhen: forcing photography into two brand colours

name: Gradient
definition: A fill that transitions between two or more colours across a shape, defined by colour stops and by the space the transition is interpolated in.
useWhen: a fill that changes colour across its own area

name: Color stop
definition: A colour pinned at a position along a gradient, with an optional hint between two stops that moves the halfway point of the transition off centre.
useWhen: pinning a colour at a point along a gradient
notes: Interpolation hint is genuine tail vocabulary and could be split out.

name: Conic gradient
definition: A gradient whose colours sweep around a centre point like a clock hand rather than along a line, the shape behind pie charts, colour wheels and progress rings.
useWhen: colours sweeping around a centre instead of across a line

name: Mesh gradient
definition: A soft multi-point blend built from colours placed on a grid and smoothed between them, giving the blurred, cloudlike backgrounds a linear gradient cannot.
useWhen: a soft multi-point colour blend, not a straight ramp
notes: Tail gold: a very common visual with no name most designers can produce on demand.

name: Color interpolation
definition: The rule for what happens between two colours in a gradient or transition, including which space the blend runs in and which way around the hue wheel it travels.
useWhen: controlling the path a blend takes between two colours
notes: Tail gold: names why blue to yellow goes through grey in sRGB but not in OKLCH.

name: Color banding
definition: The visible stripes that appear across a gradient when a display or file cannot render enough intermediate steps to keep the transition smooth.
useWhen: a gradient breaking into visible stripes
notes: Tail gold and highly demoable: one wide, low-contrast gradient shows it immediately.

name: Dithering
definition: Adding fine noise to a gradient or image so the eye averages neighbouring pixels into the missing intermediate colours, hiding the bands.
useWhen: removing banding by adding fine noise

name: Hue shift
definition: Rotating hue deliberately along a ramp, warmer at the light end and cooler at the dark end, so a scale looks alive instead of like one colour fading out.
useWhen: steering hue across a ramp instead of holding it fixed

sources.title: Rampensau: palette generation with hue cycling

notes: Tail gold: names the trick behind ramps that look designed rather than generated.

name: Dynamic color
definition: A scheme generated at runtime from a source the user controls, such as a wallpaper, so the product's palette is derived on the device rather than shipped.
useWhen: the palette is generated on the device, not shipped

sources.title: Material 3: dynamic color from a user-generated source

resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of material-you

name: Seed color
definition: The single input colour an algorithm expands into a whole scheme, so a palette becomes something derived from one decision rather than picked swatch by swatch.
useWhen: one colour in, a whole palette out

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

name: Color harmonization
definition: Nudging an outside colour's hue toward the current scheme so a fixed brand or status colour sits inside a generated palette without looking imported.
useWhen: making a fixed outside colour belong to a generated scheme
notes: Tail gold: the answer to 'my warning orange clashes with the generated theme'.

name: Color token
definition: A named colour decision stored once and referenced everywhere, so retheming is a change to the value rather than an edit at every place it is used.
useWhen: a colour stored as a name so it can be repointed

name: Primitive color token
definition: A raw palette value named for what it is, like blue-500, sitting under the semantic layer that names colours for what they do.
useWhen: the raw palette value beneath a semantic name

sources.title: Color token naming: primitive, semantic and component layers

notes: Component-level tokens are a third tier; may deserve a separate entry outside the color category.

name: Swatch
definition: A small block of flat colour shown as a sample, used in pickers and documentation to stand in for a value the reader cannot otherwise see.
useWhen: a small block standing in for a colour value

name: Eyedropper
definition: A tool that turns the cursor into a sampler so a colour can be picked from anywhere on screen, usually with a magnified preview of the pixel under it.
useWhen: sampling a colour from pixels rather than typing a value
notes: Cross-category: recorded as component, surfaced by the colour sweep. Merge with the component file's color-picker entry if one exists.

name: Color picker
definition: A control for choosing a colour, usually pairing a saturation and lightness field with a hue slider, an alpha slider and a text field for a value.
useWhen: letting a person choose an arbitrary colour
notes: Cross-category: component, not color. Likely a duplicate of a record from the component sweep.

name: currentColor
definition: A CSS keyword meaning the element's own text colour, letting borders, icons and fills inherit whatever colour the surrounding text happens to be.
useWhen: an icon or border that should follow the text colour
notes: Tail gold for icon systems: one keyword is why an SVG picks up a button's text colour.

name: color-mix()
definition: A CSS function that blends two colours by a chosen percentage in a chosen colour space, so hover and disabled variants are derived rather than hand-picked.
useWhen: deriving a variant from a colour instead of picking one

sources.title: CSS Color Module Level 5 vocabulary in css-color-4

name: Relative color syntax
definition: CSS notation that builds a new colour from an existing one by naming an origin colour with from and then adjusting individual channels.
useWhen: deriving a colour by editing one channel of another

name: contrast-color()
definition: A CSS function that returns a foreground colour guaranteed to contrast with a given background, moving the on-colour decision from the palette into the browser.
useWhen: asking the browser for a readable foreground
notes: Renamed from the earlier color-contrast() proposal; both names are searched.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of on-color, which carries "contrast color"

name: System color keyword
definition: A CSS keyword such as Canvas, CanvasText or LinkText that resolves to a colour chosen by the operating system rather than by the page.
useWhen: styling with the colours the OS itself picked

sources.title: Windows High Contrast Mode and CSS custom properties

name: Named color
definition: One of the CSS keywords such as tomato or rebeccapurple that map to fixed sRGB values, a fossil vocabulary still useful for prototypes and debugging.
useWhen: the keyword colours built into CSS

name: Sequential palette
definition: A data palette that runs light to dark in one direction, encoding an ordered quantity so that darker always means more.
useWhen: colour encoding an ordered quantity
notes: Data visualisation vocabulary; close cousin of the existing color-ramp entry but ordered by value, not by UI job.

name: Diverging palette
definition: A data palette built from two sequential scales meeting at a neutral midpoint, used when values run above and below a meaningful zero.
useWhen: values that run above and below a midpoint

name: Categorical palette
definition: A data palette of distinct hues at roughly equal visual weight, used for groups that have no order so no colour reads as larger than another.
useWhen: colouring unordered groups without implying rank

name: Color vision deficiency
definition: Reduced ability to tell certain hues apart, most often red from green, which makes hue alone an unreliable way to carry meaning for roughly one man in twelve.
useWhen: checking a palette against reduced hue discrimination
notes: Cross-category: recorded as accessibility, surfaced by the colour sweep.

name: Color as the only cue
definition: The failure of carrying meaning in hue with nothing else, so a reader who cannot separate those hues, or is on a monochrome screen, loses the information entirely.
useWhen: checking that meaning survives without hue

sources.title: MDN: <color> notes WCAG 2.2 advice against colour as the sole cue

notes: Cross-category: accessibility. The WCAG URL follows the same pattern as the verified non-text-contrast page but was not fetched this sweep.
resolved: folded into use-of-color, which carries "color as the only cue" and "greyscale test"

name: Non-text contrast
definition: The requirement that controls, focus indicators and meaningful graphics reach 3:1 against what is next to them, which is the rule that governs borders and icons.
useWhen: contrast for controls and icons rather than text
notes: Cross-category: accessibility. Kept separate from contrast-ratio because the 3:1 threshold for controls is what people get wrong.

name: Vibrancy
definition: Apple's treatment where foreground colour samples the blurred content behind a material, so labels on a translucent panel shift with whatever they cover.
useWhen: foreground colour that reacts to the blur behind it

sources.title: Apple HIG: Dark Mode (vibrancy and materials)

notes: Related to the existing glassmorphism entry; vibrancy is the platform mechanism, glassmorphism is the aesthetic.

name: Emphasis level
definition: A hierarchy expressed by lowering the opacity of one foreground colour rather than by choosing different colours, giving high, medium and disabled text one source.
useWhen: ranking text by opacity instead of by separate colours
notes: Material 3 moved to explicit on-surface-variant roles instead; the entry should note the opacity approach can quietly fail contrast.

name: Selection color
definition: The highlight painted behind text a reader has selected, which a page can restyle and thereby break the contrast the operating system had guaranteed.
useWhen: styling the highlight behind selected text

name: Scrollbar color
definition: The thumb and track colours of a scrollbar, which a page can set explicitly or leave to the declared colour scheme so the browser draws its own dark variant.
useWhen: matching the scrollbar to a dark or branded theme
notes: Marked iframe: the honest subject is the document scroller, though a scrolling sub-element demo could stay inline.

name: Color theme
definition: A complete named set of colour values a product can swap in whole, so light, dark, high contrast and per-tenant branding are the same mechanism.
useWhen: a whole palette swapped as one named set

name: Color alias
definition: A second name pointing at an existing scale so one palette can answer to several meanings, letting yellow serve as both warning and pending without duplication.
useWhen: one scale answering to more than one meaning
notes: Merge candidate with semantic-color and primitive-color-token; the three describe one layered system from different angles.

name: Interaction color step
definition: The convention that hover, active and selected are the next steps along the same scale rather than separate colours, so states are derived from one ramp.
useWhen: hover and pressed derived from a scale, not picked
notes: Tail gold: the reason a ramp has twelve steps rather than nine. Contrasts with state-layer, which does the same job with opacity.

name: Static color
definition: A colour deliberately excluded from theming because it sits on something that never changes, such as a label over a photo or a fixed brand mark.
useWhen: a colour that must not flip with the theme
notes: Material has the parallel idea in its fixed colour roles (primary fixed, on primary fixed).

name: Outline color
definition: The role that draws boundaries, split into a stronger value for edges that must be seen and a weaker one for dividers that only need to hint at structure.
useWhen: the colour of borders and dividers as a named role

implementations.name: steps 6 to 8, borders and focus rings
